source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice mcqs written from Chapter 2 (PDF 25-36), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 2 (Computational Thinking & Algorithms) ke poore chapter se practice MCQs hain, chapter ke sections ki tarteeb mein. Har sawal ka aik sahi jawab hai aur saath mukhtasar wajah; numerical sawalon mein hal ke qadam diye gaye hain.

blocks.prompt:
1 Computational thinking is useful for:
(Computational thinking kis ke liye mufeed hai?)

options.text: har aik ke liye, sirf computer science ke students ke liye nahi

blocks.explanation: 2.1: computational thinking masail ko saaf aur mantiqi tor par hal karne ka tareeqa hai; yeh sirf computer science ke students ke liye nahi. Scientists, engineers aur chefs bhi ise istemal karte hain.

book_ref.quote: This thinking is not only for computer science students

blocks.prompt:
2 According to the chapter, chefs use computational thinking when they:
(Chapter ke mutabiq chefs computational thinking kab istemal karte hain?)
blocks.explanation: 2.1 (Tidbit): scientists, engineers aur chefs bhi pecheeda (complex) kaam plan karte waqt computational thinking istemal karte hain.

book_ref.quote: Computational thinking is used by scientists, engineers, and even chefs when planning complex tasks

blocks.prompt:
3 While thinking computationally, what do we do with the unnecessary details of a problem?
(Computational thinking mein masle ki ghair zaroori tafseel ke saath kya karte hain?)

options.text: Unhein hata kar ahem nukat par tawajjo dete hain

blocks.explanation: 2.1: computational thinking mein ghair zaroori tafseel hata kar ahem nukat par tawajjo dete hain, phir masla hal karne ke wazeh qadam banate hain.

book_ref.quote: We remove unnecessary details and focus on important points

blocks.prompt:
4 Looking for patterns in problems and solutions is a part of computational thinking known as:
(Masail aur un ke hal mein patterns dhoondna computational thinking ka kaun sa hissa hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.1: hum masail aur hal mein patterns dhoondte hain; kitabon ko subject ya size se tarteeb dena pattern recognition hai.

book_ref.quote: We look for patterns in problems and solutions

blocks.prompt:
5 The clear steps created in computational thinking can be followed by:
(Computational thinking mein banaye gaye wazeh qadam kaun follow kar sakta hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.1: hum masla hal karne ke wazeh qadam banate hain; yeh qadam insaan ya computer dono follow kar sakte hain.

book_ref.quote: These steps can be followed by humans or computers

blocks.prompt:
6 Sorting books by subject or size is a real-life example of:
(Kitabon ko subject ya size se tarteeb dena kis ki rozmarra misal hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.1: kitabon ko subject ya size se tarteeb dena pattern recognition dikhata hai.

book_ref.quote: Sorting books by subject or size shows pattern recognition

blocks.prompt:
7 Which real-life activity is given as an example of breaking tasks into smaller parts?
(Kaun si rozmarra activity kaamon ko chhote hisson mein todne ki misal hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.1: safar ki planning mein kaam chhote hisson mein toote jate hain (decomposition); kitabein tarteeb dena pattern recognition hai.

book_ref.quote: Planning a trip includes breaking tasks into smaller parts

blocks.prompt:
8 Playing strategy games uses computational thinking because it requires:
(Strategy games khelne mein computational thinking kyun hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.1: strategy games mein aage ka sochna parta hai; mobile ka masla theek karna mantiqi soch hai.

book_ref.quote: Playing strategy games requires thinking ahead

blocks.prompt:
9 Cooking a recipe is an example of computational thinking because it uses:
(Recipe pakana computational thinking ki misal kyun hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.1: recipe pakane mein qadam ba qadam hidayat hoti hain; rozana timetable banana bhi misal hai.

book_ref.quote: Cooking a recipe uses step-by-step instructions

blocks.prompt:
10 One benefit of problem solving using computational thinking is that it:
(Computational thinking se masla hal karne ka aik faida kya hai?)

options.text: ghaltiyan aur uljhan kam karta hai
qadmon ki zaroorat khatam karta hai

blocks.explanation: 2.2: computational thinking se masail mantiqi aur munazzam tareeqe se hal hote hain; is se ghaltiyan aur uljhan kam hoti hain.

book_ref.quote: It helps reduce mistakes and confusion

blocks.prompt:
11 While identifying a problem clearly, it is important to know:
(Masla wazeh tor par pehchante waqt kya jaanna zaroori hai?)

options.text: di gayi maloomat aur matloob nateeja

blocks.explanation: 2.2: humein samajhna hai ke masla kya pooch raha hai; di gayi maloomat aur matloob nateeja jaanna zaroori hai.

book_ref.quote: It is important to know the given information and the expected result

blocks.prompt:
12 Which of the following helps in understanding a problem better?
(In mein se kya masla behtar samajhne mein madad karta hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.2: saada sawal poochna masla behtar samajhne mein madad karta hai; ghair zaroori tafseel nazar andaz karni chahiye.

book_ref.quote: Asking simple questions helps in understanding the problem better

blocks.prompt:
13 Identifying a problem clearly helps to:
(Masla wazeh pehchanna kis cheez mein madad karta hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.2: wazeh masla durust hal ki taraf le jata hai; yeh qadam waqt aur mehnat bachata hai.

book_ref.quote: This step helps save time and effort

blocks.prompt:
14 Why is a big problem broken into smaller parts?
(Bare masle ko chhote hisson mein kyun toda jata hai?)

options.text: Chhote hisson mein zyada mehnat lagti hai
Chhote hisse samajhne aur sambhalne mein aasan hain

blocks.explanation: 2.2: bara masla aik dam hal karna mushkil hota hai; chhote hisse samajhne aur sambhalne mein aasan hain, aur har hissa qadam ba qadam hal hota hai.

book_ref.quote: A big problem can be difficult to solve at once

blocks.prompt:
15 Decomposition allows us to:
(Decomposition humein kya karne deti hai?)

options.text: aik waqt mein aik kaam par tawajjo

blocks.explanation: 2.2: decomposition (todna) soch ko munazzam karti aur aik waqt mein aik kaam par tawajjo dene deti hai; is se uljhan aur pareshani kam hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: It allows us to focus on one task at a time

blocks.prompt:
16 Which statement about the steps of an algorithm is correct?
(Algorithm ke qadmon ke baare mein kaun sa bayan durust hai?)

options.text: Sirf computer follow kar sakta hai
Har qadam saaf ho aur qadam sahi tarteeb mein hon

blocks.explanation: 2.2: har qadam saaf aur aasan ho aur qadam sahi tarteeb mein hon; is se ghaltiyan rukti hain.

book_ref.quote: The steps must be in the correct order

blocks.prompt:
17 When each step of a solution is clear, simple and in the correct order:
(Jab hal ka har qadam saaf, saada aur sahi tarteeb mein ho to:)

options.text: sirf likhne wala follow kar sakta hai
koi bhi qadmon ko aasani se samajh aur istemal kar sakta hai

blocks.explanation: 2.2: saaf aur tarteeb wale qadmon wale hal (algorithms) ghaltiyan rokte hain, aur koi bhi in qadmon ko aasani se samajh aur istemal kar sakta hai; computer bhi qadam ba qadam hidayat follow karte hain.

book_ref.quote: Anyone can understand and use the steps easily

blocks.prompt:
18 Which activity shows whether a solution works properly?
(Kaun sa amal dikhata hai ke hal theek kaam karta hai ya nahi?)
blocks.explanation: 2.2: hal milne ke baad us ki jaanch hoti hai; hal ko test karna dikhata hai ke woh theek chalta hai ya nahi.

book_ref.quote: Testing the solution shows whether it works properly

blocks.prompt:
19 A solution can be improved by making it:
(Hal ko kis tarah behtar banaya ja sakta hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.2: hal ko zyada saada ya tez bana kar behtar kiya ja sakta hai; is se karkardagi behtar hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: We can improve the solution by making it simpler or faster

blocks.text: 2.3 Logic as a Knowledge Representation Framework

blocks.prompt:
20 Logic is described in the chapter as:
(Chapter mein logic ko kya kaha gaya hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.3: logic sahi istidlal (reasoning) ki science hai aur computer science ka ahem tasawwur hai.

book_ref.quote: Logic is the science of true reasoning

blocks.prompt:
21 As a knowledge representation framework, logic helps to:
(Knowledge representation framework ke tor par logic kis cheez mein madad karta hai?)

options.text: pecheeda maloomat ko saade tareeqe se dikhana

blocks.explanation: 2.3: logic computers ko maloomat sahi store karne, samajhne aur istemal karne mein madad deta hai; is se pecheeda maloomat saade tareeqe se dikhayi ja sakti hai.

book_ref.quote: Using logic, complex information can be represented in a simple way

blocks.prompt:
22 In programs and algorithms, logical statements help to:
(Programs aur algorithms mein logical statements kis kaam aate hain?)
blocks.explanation: 2.3: logical statements programs aur algorithms mein istemal hote hain aur program ke flow (chalne ki tarteeb) ko control karte hain.

book_ref.quote: These statements help control the flow of programs

blocks.prompt:
23 In computer science, logic helps computers to understand:
(Computer science mein logic computers ko kya samajhne mein madad deta hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.3: computer science mein logic ka matlab rules se sahi faisle karna hai; yeh computers ko true aur false conditions samjhata hai.

book_ref.quote: Logic helps computers understand true and false conditions

blocks.prompt:
24 Logic-based decision making is used in:
(Logic par mabni faisle kahan istemal hote hain?)
blocks.explanation: 2.3: logic faislon ko yaksan aur durust banata hai; yeh expert systems aur artificial intelligence mein istemal hota hai.

book_ref.quote: It is used in expert systems and artificial intelligence

blocks.prompt:
25 Using logic, decisions are made based on facts and rules. This:
(Logic se faisle haqaiq aur rules par hote hain. Is se:)

options.text: uljhan aur andaza khatam hota hai

blocks.explanation: 2.3: logic se faisle haqaiq aur rules par hote hain; yeh uljhan aur andazay ko khatam karta hai.

book_ref.quote: It removes confusion and guesswork

blocks.prompt:
26 "If it rains, then we will stay indoors" is an example of a:
("If it rains, then we will stay indoors" kis ki misal hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.3 (Class Activity): students school ki zindagi ke baare mein saada "if-then" statements banate hain, jaise "If it rains, then we will stay indoors."

book_ref.quote: Example: “If it rains, then we will stay indoors.”

blocks.prompt:
27 Propositional logic deals with:
(Propositional logic kis cheez se mutaliq hai?)

options.text: sirf objects aur un ki khasoosiyat
aise statements jo true ya false hon

blocks.explanation: 2.4: propositional logic logic ki bunyadi shakal hai; yeh aise statements se mutaliq hai jo true ya false hon, jinhein propositions kehte hain.

book_ref.quote: It deals with statements that can be true or false

blocks.prompt:
28 Which of the following is a proposition?
(In mein se kaun sa proposition hai?)

options.text: Lahore is a city in Punjab.

blocks.explanation: 2.4: proposition aisa bayan hai jo ya true ho ya false; sawal aur hukm propositions nahi hote.

book_ref.quote: Questions and commands are not propositions

blocks.prompt:
29 A proposition can be:
(Proposition kaisa ho sakta hai?)

options.text: aik waqt mein true aur false
ya true ya false, aik waqt mein dono nahi

blocks.explanation: 2.4: proposition ya true hota hai ya false; aik hi waqt mein dono nahi ho sakta.

book_ref.quote: It cannot be both true and false at the same time

blocks.prompt:
30 A proposition is usually represented by:
(Proposition ko aam tor par kis se zahir kiya jata hai?)

options.text: capital letter jaise P, Q ya R

blocks.explanation: 2.4: proposition aam tor par bare harf (capital letter) jaise P, Q ya R se likha jata hai, maslan P = "The sky is blue".

book_ref.quote: A proposition is usually represented by a capital letter, such as P, Q, or R

blocks.prompt:
31 Which of the following is a simple proposition?
(In mein se kaun sa simple proposition hai?)

options.text: The library is open and it is quiet.
The shop is closed or it is Sunday.
It is hot and it is sunny.

blocks.explanation: 2.4: simple proposition mein sirf aik bayan hota hai aur woh mazeed toota nahi ja sakta; baqi do bayanat ko connective se jorte hain.

book_ref.quote: A simple proposition contains only one statement

blocks.prompt:
32 Two or more simple propositions are joined into a compound proposition by:
(Do ya zyada simple propositions ko compound proposition mein kis se joda jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.4: compound proposition do ya zyada simple propositions mila kar banta hai; inhein logical connectives se joda jata hai.

book_ref.quote: Logical connectives are used to join them

blocks.prompt:
33 The connective used when both statements must be true is:
(Jab dono bayanat ka true hona zaroori ho to kaun sa connective istemal hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.4: AND tab jab dono bayan true hon; OR tab jab kam az kam aik true ho; NOT sach ko ulat deta hai.

book_ref.quote: AND is used when both statements must be true

blocks.prompt:
34 If P is True, then NOT P is:
(Agar P True ho to NOT P kya hoga?)
blocks.explanation: 2.4: NOT bayan ki sachai ko ulat deta hai, is liye NOT True = False.

book_ref.quote: NOT is used to reverse the truth of a statement

blocks.prompt:
35 P = "It is Friday" is False and Q = "It is a holiday" is True. The truth value of P OR Q is:
(P = "It is Friday" False aur Q = "It is a holiday" True hai. P OR Q ki truth value kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.4: OR tab true hai jab kam az kam aik bayan true ho; Q true hai, is liye P OR Q True hai.

book_ref.quote: OR is used when at least one statement is true

blocks.prompt:
36 P is True and Q is False. The truth value of P AND Q is:
(P True aur Q False hai. P AND Q ki truth value kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.4: AND sirf tab true hai jab dono true hon; Q false hai, is liye P AND Q False hai.

book_ref.quote: These connectives help form compound propositions

blocks.prompt:
37 How many rows does a truth table need for an expression with three propositions P, Q and R?
(Teen propositions P, Q aur R wale expression ke truth table mein kitni rows hongi?)
blocks.explanation: 2.5: truth tables tamam mumkina combinations likhte hain, n propositions ke liye 2^n rows; 2^3 = 8.

book_ref.quote: Truth tables enumerate all possible combinations (2ⁿ rows for n propositions)

blocks.prompt:
38 The truth value of a compound proposition is determined by:
(Compound proposition ki truth value kis se tay hoti hai?)

options.text: us ke hisson ki truth values se

blocks.explanation: 2.5: compound proposition ki truth value us ke hisson (components) ki values se tay hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: Truth value of a compound proposition is determined by the values of its components

blocks.prompt:
39 The first step in creating a truth table is to:
(Truth table banane ka pehla qadam kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.5: truth table propositions pehchanne se shuru hota hai; phir tamam combinations likhe jate hain, connectives qadam ba qadam lagaye jate hain aur har row ka nateeja likha jata hai.

book_ref.quote: Creating a truth table starts with identifying the propositions

blocks.prompt:
40 After listing all combinations of truth values in a truth table, the next step is to:
(Truth table mein tamam combinations likhne ke baad agla qadam kya hai?)

options.text: logical connectives qadam ba qadam lagana

blocks.explanation: 2.5: tamam combinations likhne ke baad logical connectives qadam ba qadam lagaye jate hain aur har row ka nateeja likha jata hai.

book_ref.quote: Logical connectives are applied step by step

blocks.prompt:
41 In the truth table of Figure 2.5, for which combination is A OR B False?
(Figure 2.5 ke truth table mein A OR B kis combination par False hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.5: table dikhata hai ke A OR B har row mein True hai siwaye A = False, B = False ke.

book_ref.quote: It shows the final result for each combination

blocks.prompt:
42 For the rows (A, B) = TT, TF, FT, FF, the column of (A AND B) OR (NOT A) is:
(Rows (A, B) = TT, TF, FT, FF ke liye (A AND B) OR (NOT A) ka column kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.5: TT: T OR F = T; TF: F OR F = F; FT: F OR T = T; FF: F OR T = T.

book_ref.quote: A truth table lists all possible combinations of truth values

blocks.prompt:
43 Which of the following is a purpose of truth tables?
(In mein se truth tables ka maqsad kaun sa hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.5: truth tables dikhate hain ke expression kaisa bartao karta hai, kab true ya false hai, aur mukhtalif statements ka muqabla karne mein madad dete hain.

book_ref.quote: They help compare different logical statements

blocks.prompt:
44 Truth tables help in logical reasoning because they:
(Truth tables logical reasoning mein kyun madadgar hain?)

options.text: kuch input values chhor dete hain

blocks.explanation: 2.5: truth tables tamam mumkina input values likhte hain aur logical reasoning mein uljhan door karte hain.

book_ref.quote: They help remove confusion in logical reasoning

blocks.prompt:
45 The symbol used to show that two logical expressions are equivalent is:
(Do logical expressions ke equivalent hone ka nishan kaun sa hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.6: equivalence ke liye nishan ≡ hai; ∀ aur ∃ quantifiers hain.

book_ref.quote: The symbol “≡” is used to show equivalence

blocks.prompt:
46 Two logical expressions are equivalent when they:
(Do logical expressions kab equivalent hote hain?)

options.text: kam az kam aik case mein true hon
har case mein truth values aik hon

blocks.explanation: 2.6: expressions mukhtalif dikhein tab bhi nateeja aik ho sakta hai; agar har case mein truth values aik hon to woh equivalent hain.

book_ref.quote: Even if expressions look different, they may give the same result

blocks.prompt:
47 Which pair of expressions is equivalent (checked over all four rows of a truth table)?
(Kaun si jori equivalent hai (truth table ki chaaron rows par check karke)?)

options.text: NOT (A AND B) and (NOT A) AND (NOT B)
A AND B and A OR B
NOT (A OR B) and (NOT A) AND (NOT B)

blocks.explanation: 2.6: TT, TF, FT, FF ke liye NOT (A OR B) = F, F, F, T aur (NOT A) AND (NOT B) = F, F, F, T; har case mein milte hain. NOT (A AND B) = F, T, T, T, jo mukhtalif hai.

book_ref.quote: Each expression is tested for all possible truth values

blocks.prompt:
48 Besides truth tables, equivalence can also be identified by using:
(Truth tables ke ilawa equivalence kis cheez se pehchani ja sakti hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.6: equivalent expressions truth tables se pehchane jate hain; logical laws (mantiqi qawaneen) bhi equivalence pehchanne aur expressions saada karne mein madad dete hain.

book_ref.quote: Logical laws can also help identify equivalence

blocks.prompt:
49 In programming, replacing an expression by a simpler equivalent one:
(Programming mein kisi expression ko saade equivalent se badalne se:)
blocks.explanation: 2.6: equivalence pecheeda expressions ko saade se badalne deti hai; programming mein is se code ki efficiency barhti hai.

book_ref.quote: In programming, equivalent expressions improve code efficiency

blocks.prompt:
50 Which of these is a benefit of equivalence in logic?
(Logic mein equivalence ka aik faida kaun sa hai?)

options.text: Har expression ko true bana deti hai
Truth tables ki zaroorat khatam kar deti hai
Propositions ko sawal bana deti hai

blocks.explanation: 2.6: equivalence mantiqi ghaltiyon se bachati hai aur sahi reasoning aur faisle yaqeeni banati hai.

book_ref.quote: Equivalence helps avoid logical errors

blocks.prompt:
51 Propositional satisfiability is important for:
(Propositional satisfiability kis ke liye ahem hai?)

options.text: algorithms design karna aur programs verify karna

blocks.explanation: 2.7: satisfiability logical statements test karne aur faisle karne mein madad deti hai; yeh algorithms design karne aur programs verify karne ke liye ahem hai.

book_ref.quote: It is important for designing algorithms and verifying programs

blocks.prompt:
52 "You must bring pizza AND you must NOT bring pizza" is:
("You must bring pizza AND you must NOT bring pizza" kya hai?)

options.text: satisfiable, kyun ke pizza laya gaya
unsatisfiable, kyun ke koi hal nahi

blocks.explanation: 2.7: "pizza lao AND pizza mat lao" kabhi true nahi ho sakta, koi hal nahi: yeh unsatisfiable expression hai.

book_ref.quote: Result: No solution exists = unsatisfiable expression.

blocks.prompt:
53 For "Bring pizza OR (burger AND do NOT bring soda)", which choice makes the expression true?
("Bring pizza OR (burger AND do NOT bring soda)" ke liye kaun sa intikhab expression ko true banata hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.7: pizza lane se OR ka aik hissa true ho jata hai, is liye "pizza, soda nahi" hal hai aur expression satisfiable hai.

book_ref.quote: Result: Bring pizza, no soda = satisfiable expression. Solution exists.

blocks.prompt:
54 A proposition that is false for every possible combination of truth values is:
(Jo proposition har mumkina combination par false ho, woh kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.7: proposition satisfiable hai agar kam az kam aik combination use true kare; agar sab combinations false karein to woh unsatisfiable hai.

book_ref.quote: If all possible combinations make it false, it is unsatisfiable

blocks.prompt:
55 Satisfiability of a proposition depends on:
(Proposition ki satisfiability kis par munhasir hai?)

options.text: sirf capital letters ki tadad par
expression ki banawat aur connectives par

blocks.explanation: 2.7: satisfiability expression ki banawat aur istemal hue logical connectives (AND, OR, NOT) par munhasir hai.

book_ref.quote: Satisfiability depends on the structure of the expression and the logical connectives used

blocks.prompt:
56 One way to test whether a proposition is satisfiable is to:
(Proposition satisfiable hai ya nahi, test karne ka aik tareeqa kya hai?)

options.text: truth table se tamam cases check karna
sirf aik be-tarteeb case check karna

blocks.explanation: 2.7: truth table se tamam mumkina cases check karna satisfiability test karne ka aik tareeqa hai.

book_ref.quote: Checking all possible cases using a truth table is one way to test satisfiability

blocks.prompt:
57 Which of the following expressions is unsatisfiable?
(In mein se kaun sa expression unsatisfiable hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.7: P AND NOT P kabhi true nahi kyun ke P aik saath true aur false nahi ho sakta; baqi kam az kam aik case mein true hain.

book_ref.quote: This is never true because P cannot be both true and false

blocks.prompt:
58 "P AND Q" is satisfiable because it is true when:
("P AND Q" satisfiable hai kyun ke yeh tab true hai jab:)

options.text: P aur Q dono true hon
P aur Q dono false hon

blocks.explanation: 2.7: P AND Q tab true hai jab P aur Q dono true hon, is liye is ka kam az kam aik true nateeja hai aur yeh satisfiable hai.

book_ref.quote: Another example is “P AND Q,” which is true when both P and Q are true

blocks.prompt:
59 Is the expression (A AND NOT A) OR B satisfiable?
(Kya expression (A AND NOT A) OR B satisfiable hai?)

options.text: Nahi, kyun ke A AND NOT A false hai
Haan, jab bhi B true ho yeh true hai
Ise check nahi kiya ja sakta

blocks.explanation: 2.7: A AND NOT A hamesha false hai, is liye expression ki value B jaisi hai; TT aur FT par true hai, yani kam az kam aik true nateeja: satisfiable.

book_ref.quote: Satisfiable expressions have at least one true outcome, while unsatisfiable expressions have none

blocks.prompt:
60 Predicate logic is:
(Predicate logic kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.8: predicate logic, propositional logic ki tausee (extension) hai; yeh objects aur un ki khasoosiyat ke baare mein zyada tafseeli bayan karti hai.

book_ref.quote: Predicate logic is an extension of propositional logic

blocks.prompt:
61 "x is greater than 5" is a predicate because:
("x is greater than 5" predicate kyun hai?)

options.text: is ki sachai x ki value par munhasir hai

blocks.explanation: 2.8: predicate aisa bayan hai jo variables ki values ke mutabiq true ya false ho; "x is greater than 5" x par munhasir hai.

book_ref.quote: “x is greater than 5” is a predicate because it depends on x

blocks.prompt:
62 For the predicate "x is greater than 5", which value of x makes it true?
(Predicate "x is greater than 5" ke liye x ki kaun si value ise true banati hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.8: "x is greater than 5" sirf tab true hai jab x > 5; 8 > 5 true hai, jab ke 5, 3 aur 0, 5 se bare nahi.

book_ref.quote: A predicate is a statement that can be true or false depending on the values of the variables

blocks.prompt:
63 In predicate logic, variables represent:
(Predicate logic mein variables kya zahir karte hain?)

options.text: domain of discourse ke objects ya values

blocks.explanation: 2.8: variables domain of discourse (zer-e-bahas daira) ke objects ya values ko zahir karte hain; predicates objects ki khasoosiyat ya taluqat batate hain.

book_ref.quote: Variables represent objects or values in the domain of discourse

blocks.prompt:
64 The predicate isEven(x) is true for which value of x?
(Predicate isEven(x) x ki kis value par true hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.8: isEven(x) tab true hai jab x jift (even) adad ho; 14 even hai.

book_ref.quote: For example, “isEven(x)” is true if x is an even number

blocks.prompt:
65 In the predicate Tall(Ali), "Tall" and "Ali" are respectively the:
(Predicate Tall(Ali) mein "Tall" aur "Ali" tarteeb se kya hain?)
blocks.explanation: 2.8: predicate logic mein Tall(Ali) se subject Ali aur property Tall nazar aate hain; propositional logic A = "Ali is Tall" andar nahi dekh sakti.

book_ref.quote: Can see subject Ali + property Tall

blocks.prompt:
66 What is a limitation of propositional logic compared with predicate logic?
